name: 401 KAR 5:065 Section 2(5): KPDES reporting of spills, bypasses, upsets
status_reason: The only overflow-reporting rule found: report to the Division of Water, no public notice duty.
notes: Quote: "Reporting shall be as established in 40 C.F.R. 122.41 except that: (a) If a spill or release of pollutants or contaminants, bypass, upset, or other event of noncompliance occurs that may present an imminent or substantial danger to the environment or the public health or welfare, the permittee shall immediately notify the Division of Water by calling the Division of Water in Frankfort at (502) 564-3410 or the appropriate regional field office ... (b) If a report required by this subsection is made during other than normal business hours, it shall be made through the twenty-four (24) hour environmental emergency telephone number". No duty to tell the public was found in the regulation.

name: EPA SOBE extract, Kentucky rows (state electronic reporting system, ES2)
operator: U.S. EPA ECHO (data from Kentucky DOW)
waters_covered: statewide in principle; 43 rows in practice
access_detail: Daily ZIP from ECHO (no auth). On 2026-11-07 the current-version ZIP held only its metadata, so the module reads the current version of each report from the all-versions ZIP (2026-11-04 extract). 43 Kentucky reports from 37 permits, every one filed as a bypass (BYP) at a structure typed 'Other', submission type ES2 (Kentucky's own system), form sets KY-11256, KY-11276, KY-11286; started 2025-12-08 to 2026-01-08 (December 35, January 8), received December 2025 (34) and January 2026 (9); a point, a start and an end on all 43, a volume on 19. Receiving water: 'Unnamed Tributary or Unknown' on 26, 'Unnamed' on 4, a named stream or lake on 13.
cadence: daily ECHO file; Kentucky reports received a median 0 days after the start (the longest 5), and none since January 2026
status_reason: Read by the national eRule module (echo-sewer-overflow) with Kentucky in its states since 2026-11-07: the only dated, machine-readable record of Kentucky overflow reports with points, though Kentucky's system sent reports for two months only (December 2025 and January 2026).
notes: 2026-11-04 extract: 20 kept as reaching a water (13 naming it, 3 answering 'Receiving into an unnamed tributary? Yes', 4 whose text names a creek), 23 dropped (21 with no sign that a water was reached, 2 saying none was: 'No waterways impacted', 'did not reach a waterbody'). Kentucky's rules in the module: the zone by the event's point (Eastern, or Central in the forty-one western counties of 49 CFR 71.5(c)); a bypass whose description names a manhole, force main, lift or pump station or line break read as a sewer overflow; the form's placeholders read as no name; the callers', responders' and staff names in the descriptions scrubbed. Known problems: one Louisville MSD report ends 14 minutes before it starts; one incident is filed under two permits (Frankfort, 2025-12-22).

name: SD1 Wet Weather Overflow Notification Program (Northern Kentucky)
operator: Sanitation District No. 1 of Northern Kentucky
waters_covered: Ohio River, Licking River, Banklick Creek and other streams in Boone, Campbell and Kenton counties
access_detail: Page fetched (raw/sd1-wet-weather-notification-2026-11-03.html). Notifications by sign-up only (CivicPlus Notify Me); map of overflow areas PDF https://sd1.org/DocumentCenter/View/207/Local-Sewer-Overflows-PDF.
cadence: Quote: "We will only alert you during contact recreational season (May through October) when: Rainfall of 0.25 inches or more is recorded in SD1's service area, including Boone, Campbell and Kenton counties The Ohio River exceeds 38 feet"; "All advisories will remain in effect for 72 hours after rainfall or 72 hours after river levels drop below 38 feet."
status_reason: SD1's own published rule written into data/rules.json (rain_likely.fallback.by_permit.KY0021466): 0.25 inch of rain, a 72-hour caution, May to October, applied from radar rainfall at SD1's combined sewer outfalls; the Ohio River stage part (above 38 feet) is not applied. The alerts themselves reach subscribers only.
notes: SD1 posts CSO signs: "If you see these signs, avoid nearby water during and after rainfall for at least 72 hours." Its rule (0.25 inch, Ohio River 38 feet, 72 hours) matches the site's 72-hour yellow window.
